Subject: Residency questions for procurement — can you confirm pinning and cross-region handling?

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked for a short note on how Redwood handles data residency and whether we can get a contractual commitment to keep Acme data in the EU region. A few specific questions they raised:

- Can Redwood guarantee that all requests and at-rest data for an Acme tenant will be stored and processed only in the EU (region pinning)?
- Are there any cases where data could be processed outside the pinned region (backups, analytics, system migrations, warmup, vendor subprocessors)?
- If cross-region processing is possible, what legal/technical safeguards are in place (SCCs, encryption, KMS ownership)?

Procurement also asked for a list of subprocessors and a copy of the DPA. Can you send the latest DPA and subprocessor list and indicate whether we can add a strict residency clause in the contract (we're sensitive given our EU customers).

Appreciate a short reply we can share with procurement/legal.

Best,
Sara

Subject: Re: Residency questions for procurement — can you confirm pinning and cross-region handling?

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Short answers first, then details below so procurement/legal have language to copy:

- Can we pin? Yes — Redwood supports per-tenant region pinning on Hosted and Dedicated plans so requests and primary storage can be constrained to a single region (EU in your case).
- Cross-region processing? By default we avoid cross-region processing, but there are limited operational cases (failover, emergency migrations, analytics jobs for product telemetry, and certain vendor subprocessors) where we may process encrypted artifacts outside the pinned region.
- Safeguards: we offer encrypted transfers, SCCs for transfers out of the EEA, and you can choose Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) for Dedicated/Private deployments; for Hosted we can integrate with your cloud KMS in certain arrangements or use our encryption-at-rest with restricted key access.

I've attached the current DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf) and our subprocessor export (subprocessor_list_20260110.csv). The attachments show current subprocessors and our standard residency language. If Acme needs a hard "no-cross-border" clause we can discuss a contract addendum and the operational trade-offs (e.g., reduced geographic failover).

Details for procurement/legal (copyable):
- Region pinning: We can pin all customer primary request routing and primary persistent storage to the specified region. This includes embeddings, KV cache persisted snapshots, and stored audit logs.
- Backups & replication: Standard Hosted backups are kept encrypted and, by default, replicated to a geographically close failover region for durability. For hard residency commitments we can disable cross-region replication or provide an EU-only backup configuration at the cost of longer RPO/RTO and reduced failover SLA.
- Analytics/telemetry: Product analytics are pseudonymized and sampled; full payloads are never exported to third-party analytics without prior consent. Aggregated telemetry may be processed in our central analytics region. We can include a contractual restriction on raw payloads leaving the EU.
- Subprocessors: List attached. We notify customers 30 days before adding new subprocessors and provide data-flow descriptions on request.
- Key management: For Dedicated/Private we support CMKs (customer-managed keys) in supported clouds; for Hosted we support BYOK in limited configurations or provide Redwood-managed keys with access controls and audit logs.
- Legal safeguards: We rely on SCCs for transfers from the EEA where necessary and can include additional contractual protections in the DPA.

Next steps I propose: 1) Confirm Acme's required level (soft pin with failover allowed vs strict EU-only); 2) Neha (copying) can follow up with contractual language and SCC references; 3) Diego can propose the operational configuration (disable replication, CMK, etc).

Attaching the files now.

Hi Sara (and team),

I'll answer the legal/contractual pieces and confirm the typical options we offer for EU customers: 

1) BYOK/KMS: For Hosted customers we currently support BYOK integrations with AWS KMS and Azure Key Vault via our key-wrapping integration (we manage wrapped keys while you retain root key material in your KMS). For Dedicated/Private deployments customers can hold full CMKs in their environment (no Redwood access). The DPA includes our key-handling commitments and audit controls.

2) EU-only clause and failover: We do offer a strict EU-only addendum in cases where customers require it. The addendum removes cross-region replication and any routine cross-border processing, but it also limits our automated failover behavior. In the event of a verified EU-region outage we will:
  - Attempt in-region recovery first;
  - If full recovery cannot be achieved within the agreed RTO, we will notify the customer and may route new requests to a pre-approved secondary region for a limited duration under explicit incident authorization.

This is a trade-off: strict residency increases outage risk exposure and recovery time. If Acme needs 100% guarantee with no cross-border processing even during incidents, that is possible under an extra-legal warranty but carries limited support/availability SLA and operational caveats.

3) Subprocessors & SCCs: We will execute SCCs where required and are willing to identify subprocessors that will have access to clear-text payloads. Most subprocessors (monitoring, telemetry) operate on metadata or pseudonymized data. Please see the attached CSV for current details; we can produce a signed subprocessor exhibit for the contract.

4) Audit evidence: We can provide SOC2 reports, encryption configuration snapshots, and an export of recent access logs for a rolling 90-day window under NDA. For strict residency commitments we can provide a monthly residency attestation.

I'll draft suggested contract language for an EU-only addendum and share a short mutual action plan (MAP) for procurement.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Compliance, Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick technical note from ops/solutions perspective: 

- Geo-failover behavior: by default our routing will fail over to the nearest healthy region to preserve availability. For EU-only customers we can configure a strict routing policy that prevents automatic cross-region routing; instead, failover requires an explicit runbook step (approved by customer) to enable traffic to a secondary region.
- Cache/state implications: note that pinned tenants that disable replication will not have warmed KV caches in the secondary, so cold-start latency and token usage may increase if failover is ever triggered.
- Implementation options: 1) Soft-pin (default): pinned but permit auto-failover; 2) Hard-pin: no auto-failover, require manual opt-in during incident; 3) Dedicated private deployment with CMK: strongest residency and control.

If helpful I can prepare a short MAP with milestones (DPA signature, addendum, key-handling design, final ops runbook) and an estimate of potential availability impact for each option.

Thanks,
Diego
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
